How deficit-framed is a set of results?

Source: R/igf.R
frmaud.Rd

Counts how many of the indicators in a report measure distress, deficit or disparity and how many measure wellness or strength, and names any group reported on deficits alone.

Usage

frmaud(x)

Arguments

x

A welprof result, whose rows are counted by side.

Value

A list of class frmaud: bygrp (a data frame of group, wellness, distress, shrdef), shrdef overall and defonly (the groups with no wellness indicator).

Details

Walter (2016) shows that statistics about Indigenous peoples cluster around five Ds: disparity, deprivation, disadvantage, dysfunction and difference. Results built only of those describe Indigenous peoples as their problems. This audit does not measure anything about people; it measures the report: the share of its indicators that are deficit-framed, overall and per group, so a report can be balanced before it is published. Pair each gap with a strength-framed level (welprof, dualcont).

References

Walter M (2016). Data politics and Indigenous representation in Australian statistics. In Kukutai T, Taylor J (eds), Indigenous Data Sovereignty: Toward an Agenda, 79-97. ANU Press. doi:10.22459/caepr38.11.2016.05

Walter M, Andersen C (2013). Indigenous Statistics: A Quantitative Research Methodology. Left Coast Press. doi:10.4324/9781315426570

Examples

# your own table: made-up percentages for two communities, with limits
own <- data.frame(
  community = rep(c("Lakeside", "Riverbend"), each = 4),
  item = rep(c("Hopeful", "Satisfied", "Rarely hopeful", "Low satisfaction"),
             2),
  pct = c(64, 71, 12, 18, 58, 66, 16, 22),
  lo = c(59, 66, 9, 14, 52, 60, 12, 17),
  hi = c(69, 76, 15, 22, 64, 72, 20, 27)
)
frmaud(welprof(own, "community", "item", "pct", "lo", "hi",
               well = c("Hopeful", "Satisfied"),
               distress = c("Rarely hopeful", "Low satisfaction")))
#> Framing audit
#> -------------
#> Groups:              2
#> Wellness indicators: 4
#> Distress indicators: 4
#> Deficit-framed:      50%
#> 
#> By group (shrdef: the deficit-framed share)
#>     group  wellness  distress  shrdef
#>  Lakeside         2         2     0.5
#> Riverbend         2         2     0.5
#> 
#> 50% of the indicators reported are deficit-framed.
#> 
#> Walter (2016): statistics about Indigenous peoples cluster around
#> disparity, deprivation, disadvantage, dysfunction and difference.
#> This audits the report, not the people it describes.
